name: Where You Stand
tagline: You know how things really get done. You also know what you'll never do.
epigraph: A century ago, Canadian whisky was worth breaking the law for. On both sides of it.
language_row: Wren's resonance: ready (v2; reaffirmed through v4). Guest text 4-gram clean against every pour (Wren r3–r6). Gendered pronouns in y1–y4 refer to Roy Olmstead and Brandeis only, accepted by Wren and Hester. No Embury name in guest text (Wren's ruling, r6).
sources: Fact cards `_studio/fact-cards/roy-olmstead.md` (HistoryLink; *Olmstead v. United States*, 277 U.S. 438 (1928), LII, majority and dissents; *Katz v. United States* (1967); Federal Judicial Center, Hamm 2010; Humanities Washington 2023, legend-grade only) and `embury-canadian-maple.md` (David Embury, *The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks*, 1958/1961/2008 editions via archive.org OCR; Oxford Companion pdf 719, 1226). Drink: *The Flavor Matrix* pdf 137, 240; *Joy of Mixology* pdf 423; Oxford pdf 2146–2147. Room notes `work/outlaw-regular-guy/`.
names_note: Where You Stand (the room's pick, all three, r6). Flag for Robin (Hester): it would be the registry's third "stand" after *Standing By* and *Left Standing*, here meaning knowing your footing. Your Word (Hester's, then Wren's pick) set aside: it is y5's last two words and gives the position away. Also considered: Same Rules, No Exceptions, Five to Four, Straight Canadian, Not a Drop More.
open_items: FLAG: balance OUT on acid only (0.00 against the stirred band's 0.1–0.14). Embury's CANADIAN has no acid; adding citrus or vermouth would make it another drink. Tomás's proved fallback: built on one large cube in a rocks glass with 1¼–1½ tsp maple balances (29.5%, 7.06–8.17 g). Rule candidate: a `stirred-spirit` style (would also clear *Nothing to It*).
Name: third "stand" in the registry (Hester's flag).
Embury, the man, is never named or praised in guest text: Oxford pdf 719 records that he led the 1946–47 effort to keep college fraternities segregated (Wren's ruling, Hester's advice).

The bribery is owned in the reading: he took bribes as an officer and paid police as a bootlegger (FJC; the Court's statement of facts). The no-guns rule is paraphrased, never quoted; no claim it bound him first or cost him cargo.
Embury's whisky measure, stir, glass and peel aren't on the page: the 60 ml, the stir, the coupe and the orange peel are Tomás's calls. Curaçao is an unsourced value in the table.
Kept out: Holmes's "dirty business", the prison visits after McNeil Island, Elsie's broadcasts, "never cut it" (one weak source), *Katz* (dossier only).
